Computes an 8-bit integer index representing the configuration of a voxel's eight corners relative to an isolevel, determining which edges are intersected by the surface [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the process computes an 8-bit integer index representing the configuration of a voxel's eight corners relative to an isolevel to determine intersected edges. Source [S1] explicitly describes computing an '8-bit integer index' by setting bits based on whether corner densities are less than the isolevel. Source [S2] describes calculating a 'case index' (integer tensor) based on a binary mask of corner values relative to the iso-level, using the formula `cube_indices = sum((v_i < iso) * 2^i)`, which results in an integer representing the configuration. Both sources support the core mechanism described in the claim.

If $v_i = \text{iso\_level}$, the condition $v_i < \text{iso\_level}$ is false, so the bit remains 0 [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the $i$-th bit is set to 1 if the corner's density is less than the isolevel. By logical contrapositive, if the condition 'density < isolevel' is false (which occurs when density is equal to or greater than isolevel), the bit is not set to 1. Since the index is initialized to 0 and bits are only set to 1 under the specific condition, the bit remains 0 when the condition is false. The claim accurately reflects this logic.
